thread:
deploy-bot: Deployment event: release/hotpatch-2026.03.15 (artifact: hotpatch-weights-20260315-7f3a) pushed to prod canary group at 3187654321.

miguel_oncall: I’m seeing elevated canary perplexity and some weird tokenization in a few requests. Paging SRE.

amy_sre: On it. Can you drop a sample from the canary? pinging @raj_ml for model artifact details.

raj_ml: Received. Hotpatch artifact name was `hotpatch-weights-20260315-7f3a`. It was supposed to be a small fp16 correction for attention scaling — no tokenizer changes were intended.

jordan_support: Customer on a trial org reported odd completions — partial words joined: e.g., "playe r" -> "player"? also extra special-chars in numbered lists.

miguel_oncall: attaching canary outputs (redacted):
```\ninput: "Summarize the quarterly revenue"\ncanary_resp_v2: "Q1: $3.2M\\n- item 1\\n- item2"  <-- missing spacing and weird token glue\n```

amy_sre: Logs show the canary hosts loaded weightset hotpatch-weights-20260315-7f3a and tokenizer config fallback to default-tokenizer-v1. But the model metadata claims tokenization schema=v2. Mismatch.

raj_ml: That’s suspicious — the release script should have verified tokenizer checksum. I see the artifact package contains weights.bin and tokenizer_meta.json. tokenizer_meta.json shows a different hash than what production tokenizer service returned. Possible packaging mismatch.

incident-bot: Pager triggered: severity=high, impact=canary outputs corrupted, potential customer-facing risk. On-call: miguel_oncall.

leah_pm: How widespread? Any traffic routed beyond canary?

miguel_oncall: No, only canary group (~0.5% of traffic) so far. We should kill the rollout before promoting. Recommend feature-flag flip to block hotpatch rollout and rollback canary nodes to previous weightset.

amy_sre: Agreed. Action items: 1) flip feature flag `hotpatch_release_block` to ON. 2) trigger canary weight revert job. 3) run quick regression on prompt set. I’ll take 1+2.

raj_ml: I’ll investigate packaging pipeline. Hypothesis: a stale tokenizer_meta.json from an old dev branch was included; weights are intended for tokenizer-v2 but tokenizer meta points to v1 serialisation -> byte-level decode mismatch (non-canonical vocab offsets).

miguel_oncall: Leah, please notify support so we can prepare customer comms if the canary had any conversions. Jordan, can you run a query for any downstream customer requests to canary hits in last 15m?

jordan_support: Running query now. Preliminary: 12 requests from two customers, none flagged as errors but some post-processed content looks odd. I’ll mark them for review.

deploy-bot: Feature flag `hotpatch_release_block` set -> true by miguel_oncall at 3187654410.

amy_sre: Initiating canary revert: invoking rollback workflow `rollback-weightset --group canary --to v20260310`

deploy-bot: Rollback job started (job id rb-3187654422). Rolling back 12 canary hosts.

miguel_oncall: While rollback proceeds, set throttles to prevent any promotion jobs. Also, enable telemetry scrub to capture token-level diffs from canary responses for triage.

raj_ml: I pulled the package from artifact store. Confirmed tokenizer_meta.json hash mismatch: expected sha256: a3f2..., packaged: 4b9d... Looks like a CI merge where the weights builder picked up an older tokenizer manifest from cache. I’m opening a fix PR to the release pipeline to add checksum gating.

amy_sre: Rollback complete on all canary hosts at 3187654501. Health checks green. Canary perplexity back to baseline.

miguel_oncall: Good. Any customer impact confirmed? Jordan?

jordan_support: Of the 12 requests, 3 had visibly malformed output. Reached out to the two customers proactively; one replied acknowledging odd output; no data loss, but they want an RCA.

leah_pm: Okay. Move to mitigation summary: rollback succeeded, feature-flag blocked further rollout. Need action items: 1) PR to add tokenizer checksum gate (raj), 2) add artifact verification step to deploy bot to compare tokenizer hash before activating (amy/devops), 3) add canary-side assertion to failfast if tokenizer schema mismatch (raj/amy), 4) update release notes & customer comms (leah/jordan).

raj_ml: I’ll file the PR and include unit test to fail when token manifest and weight metadata mismatch.

amy_sre: I’ll update the deploy job to include a preflight tokenizer verification and add alarm rule if mismatch detected.

leah_pm: Jordan, draft a short customer note explaining rollback, no data loss, fix scheduled, ETA 48 hours for pipeline patch. Use empathetic tone.

jordan_support: Will draft and share in #customer-comms for review.

miguel_oncall: Logging incident for postmortem. Incident-bot creating incident record. Severity: P2 (could have been customer-facing), timeline captured.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03015-47 "Non-canonical tokenizer metadata in hotpatch artifact". Owner: leah_pm.

amy_sre: Follow-up: run a full artifact audit for the last 7 releases to ensure no other stale manifests slipped in. I’ll start that tomorrow.

raj_ml: Note for postmortem: Add test harness that runs small end-to-end canaries (weight load + tokenizer sanity) in the CI release pipeline — should catch this before artifact promotion.

leah_pm: Thanks all — great quick coordination. I’ll lead the postmortem and ensure actions are tracked. Closing thread after initial comms drafted. :thumbsup:
